prompt.context: The beverage department of a regional supermarket has seen a drop in revenue over the last year and has hired your firm to determine the cause of the decline and recommend ways to reverse the trend.
prompt.question: What is causing the revenue decline in the beverage department, and how should the client reverse this trend?

clarifying_info.a: A leading regional grocer within the southeastern U.S.
No, the competitive landscape has not changed in the last year.

clarifying_info.q: Is the revenue decline across all product categories or specific to beverages?
clarifying_info.a: The revenue decline is specifically within the beverage segment.

clarifying_info.q: What does the client want from us?
clarifying_info.a: The client wants to find the cause of the declining revenue and recommendations for how to stop the decline.

exhibits.title: Revenues and Costs by Beverage Category
exhibits.shows: A table of gallons sold (MM, average per store), price per gallon ($), and cost per gallon ($) for three beverage categories (Sodas, Waters, Others) in 2014 and 2015.

exhibits.title: Sodas by Brand
exhibits.shows: A table of gallons sold (MM, average per store) and revenue ($M, average per store) for three soda brands (Brand A, Brand B, Value Brand) in 2014 and 2015.

framework: Focus on revenue = price x quantity for each beverage sub-category
Segment revenue by category (Sodas, Waters, Others) to isolate where the decline originates
Drill into the declining category by sub-segment (brand level) to identify root cause
Assess pricing and volume dynamics at the brand level
Develop recommendations to reverse the decline using a structured framework (e.g., 4P's: Price, Promotion, Product, Placement)

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total revenue for each beverage category in 2014 and 2015. Which category is driving the overall decline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply Gallons x Price/gallon for each category in each year, then compare. The key insight is that Sodas revenue has declined materially while Waters and Others are flat/up, so the decline is isolated to Sodas.

math.setup: Revenue = Gallons (MM) x Price per gallon ($)
math.answer: Sodas is the only category with declining revenue (-$6M); Waters and Others are both slightly up. The overall beverage decline is driven entirely by Sodas.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the implied price per gallon for each soda brand in 2014 and 2015. What is driving the decline in soda revenue?
questions.guidance: Candidate should derive price = Revenue / Gallons for each brand. Brand A and Brand B prices are stable at $1.00/gallon. Value Brand price dropped significantly from $0.60 to $0.40/gallon, while its volume surged. The large volume shift toward a deeply discounted Value Brand is cannibalizing higher-priced Brand A volume and reducing overall soda revenue.

steps: Brand A 2015: $30M / 30MM gal = $1.00/gal  =>  No price change, but volume -20MM gal, revenue -$20M
Brand B 2015: $30M / 30MM gal = $1.00/gal  =>  No price change, volume +5MM gal, revenue +$5M
Value Brand 2015: $24M / 60MM gal = $0.40/gal  =>  Price dropped $0.20/gal, volume +35MM gal, revenue +$9M
Net soda revenue change: -$20M + $5M + $9M = -$6M (consistent with Exhibit 1)
math.answer: Value Brand's price dropped from $0.60 to $0.40/gallon, driving a large volume shift away from Brand A. Despite the volume surge in Value Brand, the steep price cut more than offsets the gain, and overall soda revenue falls $6M. Brand A loses $20M in revenue while Value Brand only gains $9M.

brainstorming.prompt: The client would like to hear your recommendations for how to reverse the decline in revenue of the beverage segment.

categories.name: Price
ideas: Raise the price of Value Brand back toward the $0.60/gal level to reduce cannibalization of Brand A
Introduce tiered pricing to maintain value positioning while protecting margin
Consider dynamic or promotional pricing only for specific periods rather than a permanent price cut

categories.name: Promotion
ideas: Promote Brand A with targeted discounts or loyalty rewards to win back lost volume
Bundle promotions (e.g., Brand A + snacks) to drive traffic to premium brands
Increase in-store visibility and sampling for Brand A and Brand B

categories.name: Product
ideas: Introduce new SKUs or flavors for Brand A to differentiate from Value Brand
Improve packaging or branding of Brand A to justify premium price
Evaluate whether Value Brand should remain in the portfolio or be repositioned

categories.name: Placement
ideas: Improve shelf placement of Brand A (eye-level, end-caps) versus Value Brand
Use shelf space allocation to limit visibility of Value Brand relative to premium brands
Create distinct shelf zones to reduce direct price comparison between brands

recommendation: Adjust the price of the Value Brand upward to reduce cannibalization of Brand A and recover overall soda revenue
Improve differentiation between Brand A and the Value Brand through product, packaging, and placement strategies to justify the price premium for Brand A
risks: Raising Value Brand price may alienate price-sensitive customers who have shifted to it, leading to volume loss with no revenue recovery
Any changes to Brand A or Brand B pricing could alienate those suppliers
Consumers may perceive price increase as opportunistic and shift to competing stores
next_steps: Explore optimal pricing strategy for Value Brand (e.g., price elasticity analysis)
Explore bundling opportunities to increase sales of Brand A and Brand B
Explore marketing and promotional activities to differentiate Value Brand from Brand A and Brand B
Explore shelf placement optimization of Value Brand versus premium brands
